newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes higher but shy of resistance.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes higher but shy of resistance.

text.p: Bullish supply and demand data kept prices firmer throughout the session but could not inspire the benchmark July contract to cross its upside target of 73.00 cents by the close.
The failure to break the key level discouraged traders, who said July could fall back towards support pegged at 71.90 cents on Friday, ahead of the long Memorial Day weekend.
"Where we close tomorrow is critical," Tom Reardon, a floor broker with with J&R Futures and Options, said.

He said the speculators could begin to cover short positions or take profits next week if July breaks 73.00. A settlement closer to support, however, could prompt the speculators to roll short positions into October.
"It's becoming a time factor," Reardon said, noting that slightly more than two weeks remain until the first notice day for July. "Right now the market feels a little heavy."
The benchmark July contract closed up 0.23 cent at 72.60 cents, having ranged from 72.80 to 72.42 cents. New-crop December ended 0.33 cent firmer at 74.85 cents.

Prices traded firmer from the open, when steady fund buying emerged on the heels of positive consumption and export data. But trade scale-up selling limited gains below 73.00 cents, while options activity put additional pressure on the market, traders said.
The U.S. Commerce Department put consumption at an annualized 10.96 million 480-lb bales in April, compared with an adjusted rate of 10.58 million bales in March.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged new sales of upland cotton for the week ended May 15 at a brisk 112,100 bales in the old crop, and at 86,400 bales in the new crop.
Volume was estimated at 6,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official 5,387 lots.
